tariff_level: The US should have few or no tariffs, because free trade benefits most people.
Tariffs should be low and used mainly against countries that break trade rules.
The US should put moderate tariffs on many goods to protect key industries.
The US should put high tariffs on most imports to bring manufacturing back, even if prices rise.
tariff_price_tradeoff: I wouldn't accept tariffs that raise prices about 10%; lower prices matter more than those factory jobs.
I'd accept tariffs to protect factory jobs only if prices rose around 2% to 3%, not 10%.
I'd accept tariffs that raise prices of cars and appliances about 10% to protect US factory jobs.
tariff_authority: Only Congress should set tariffs, by passing laws.
Congress should set tariffs, but a president can add them in a true emergency.
A president should be able to set tariffs whenever the president judges it's in the national interest.
tariff_authority_cases: A president should need Congress to do this: {case}.
A president should be able to do this without a vote of Congress: {case}.
trade_agreements: The US should sign agreements lowering tariffs with as many countries as possible.
The US should sign agreements lowering tariffs only if they include strong labor and environmental rules.
The US should sign agreements lowering tariffs only with close allies.
The US shouldn't sign new trade agreements, and should leave existing ones where it can.
trade_jobs_tradeoff: Trade deals that open foreign markets are worth it even if some US industries and regions lose jobs.
Those trade deals are worth it only with major help for workers who lose their jobs.
Protecting existing US jobs comes before trade deals that open foreign markets.
china_trade: The US should trade freely with China, as with any other country.
The US should limit only sales of sensitive technology to China, like advanced chips and military goods.
The US should limit sensitive technology and also move production of essentials like medicines and electronics out of China.
The US should cut off most trade with China.
china_ownership: Chinese companies should be able to own US businesses, farmland and apps like any foreign company.
Chinese companies can own US businesses, except in sensitive areas like defense and personal data.
Chinese companies shouldn't own US farmland, key technology or popular apps, but other businesses are fine.
Chinese companies shouldn't be allowed to own any US business.
industrial_policy: The government should pay companies to build factories in many US industries.
The government should pay companies to build factories only in industries vital to national security, like computer chips.
The government shouldn't pay companies to build factories; the market should decide.
buy_american: Federal agencies should buy the best value, American-made or not.
Federal agencies should have to buy American only for military and security needs.
Federal agencies should buy American unless it costs more than about 25% extra.
Federal agencies should always buy American, even at much higher cost.
offshoring_penalty: Companies that move US jobs abroad should be penalized, for example with higher taxes and losing government contracts.
Companies that move jobs abroad shouldn't be penalized, but tax breaks that make it cheaper should end.
Companies should decide where to operate, with no penalty for moving jobs abroad.
export_controls: US companies should be free to sell advanced technology like top chips to anyone, including China and Russia.
The US should block sales to rivals only for technology with clear military uses.
The US should block sales of most advanced technology to rivals, even if US companies lose sales.
friend_shoring: Allies like Canada, Japan and European countries should pay clearly lower tariffs than other countries.
Allies should pay somewhat lower tariffs than other countries.
All trading partners should be treated the same, allies or not.
Allies should face tariffs too if they sell more to us than they buy from us.
